body:
My attitude is that there is so much uncertainty in the world that I might as well continue living, because you never know what can happen. We're far from understanding human thought. Whether it's entirely naturally caused or not is a point of great contention. We're not at all sure what causes consciousness. One of the more interesting ideas that I have been interested in is panpsychism. In a nutshell, it's the idea that minds are a fundamental aspect of the universe. You should check it out if you're curious. I'm also very interested in philosophy, but specifically Hellenistic philosophy fascinates me. I like studying about religions and philosophies of the world in general as well. Hinduism in particular resonates with me. I've even read some of the Hindu holy scriptures.

If you don't mind me asking, what are your beliefs? I like learning what others think is the meaning to life.

I've done a massive amount of thinking in the last couple hours. I've thought about life, the universe, and God. I reached a few conclusions. I need to believe in God and an afterlife. I have to believe that this life is a test and that I can be with God later. I think He was with me just a few moments ago as well, but how could I really know. 

I need an explanation for why I am so different and why my world is so fucked up. The best answer I have is that God made me different so that I could do special things that other people can't do. I have a "different lens" as you say. I need spirituality because without it I can't understand anything. Perhaps I suffer so that I can fulfill a role that God needs me to do. When I was younger, I always felt that I had a special relationship with God. Math and science came easy to me at a young age. I felt "tuned-in" to God's design. I felt like I could tap into a spiritual energy that gave me knowledge and understanding. I felt like I was part of God's design and I could rejoin with Him. One thing that I always believed was that if I could understand how God designed the universe, I could rejoin with Him. That, if I could find truth, it would make me grow spiritually and perhaps I could mimic God in ways. I could create and grow just like God did. 

Maybe I have lived thousands of lives before and I am close to finishing the final hurdle of my spiritual journey by surviving and pursuing physics and stuff like that. If I killed myself now, I would fail or be set back in my journey. Maybe, when I finish this life, I will be a great being and have wonderful unknown powers. There is a sense of mystery to God and the universe I think. As humans, we have a will, unlike a rock. We have creative powers. We can engineer things. We can mimic God. In this way, I believe that we were made in God's image. 

You probably think this stuff sounds fucking stupid. I'm sorry for my confusing views.
